name: get_pull_request_requirements
description: Read what an open Origin-hosted pull request needs before it can merge, as Origin evaluates it at headSha. Each requirement has a stable id, a status (satisfied, unsatisfied, pending or unknown) and a reason; owner rules also say whether a human approval is required. A satisfied requirement says what satisfied it in satisfiedBy.kind: person_approval (a person approved with their own credentials), bot_approval (a bot or an app did), delegated_approval (a user approved through an app's or a bot's credentials), automation_approval (an automation the policy delegates its review to), approval (approved, and the evaluation does not say by which kind of approver), risk_rating (its risk rating passed it without a review), author_owned, nothing_required, exemption, checks, gate_report, and, on agentic_owners and code_review_gate, owner_rules (requirementIds names the owner rules that decided it and kinds lists what satisfied them) or not_itemized (Origin lists no owner rules that say how). satisfiedBy.approvals names each approval the rule credits by actor (user, bot or app, with its user_, sa_ or app_ id), with performedVia for a user who approved through an app or a bot, and the version it was given on: versionNumber, versionHeadSha, and atHead, which is whether that version's head is headSha. It is absent when a person other than an owner or a delegated automation cleared the rule, since the evaluation does not name them. A bot's approval can satisfy an Agentic Owners policy: one the policy lists as a bot owner satisfies it even when it requires human review, and a delegated automation only when it does not. approvalSummary reads this pull request's own review records, not those of pull requests below it, so it holds whether or not any owner rule is listed: personApprovalCounted is whether Origin counts an approval a person gave with their own credentials, personApprovalAtHead is whether one was given on headSha, and approvals lists every counted approval with the requirements that credit it. An approval stays counted across pushes until it is dismissed or replaced, so one given on an earlier version is counted and reads atHead false. A caller that cannot read the pull request's reviews still gets every satisfiedBy.kind, personApprovalCounted and personApprovalAtHead, and no approver: approvalSummary.identitiesWithheld is then reviews_read_required, and approvals is left out there and on every satisfiedBy, which says nothing about whether an approval counts. requirements covers everything a merge enforces, read from the evaluation merge_pull_request runs: when every requirement is satisfied, a merge of this head is not refused for a rule, a blocker or a bypass it would have to ask for; the merge queue's own state is not part of it. A status_checks requirement is one required status checks rule, with every check it requires in checks: its name, its status at headSha (passing, pending, failing, action_required, missing when no run reported at this head, or never_passes for the Code Review Gate, which is not a status check) and the run's detailsUrl when it has one and you can read the repository's checks. When a check reads never_passes, do not rerun it or try to fix it: tell the person that the rule has to stop requiring that check. A blocker requirement is any other mergeability blocker, such as a draft, a merge conflict, a requested change, an unresolved review thread, a branch behind its base, a stack that needs a restack or a merge freeze, with its kind in blockerKind. A ruleset_bypass requirement is a rule that fails and that only your ruleset bypass lifts; it stays unsatisfied, since a merge has to ask for the bypass. Requirements of open pull requests below this one carry their own pullNumber. actors pages the users and bots who can clear each open requirement, and excludedFrom says why someone cannot, such as being the author. Policies name users by @handle and group rosters by user_ id, so one person can appear once each way. completeness is complete, partial or pending, and incomplete says what is missing. personalGates lists the author's personal gates with each one's mode and status at head; they never count toward requirements. splitPlan is Origin's suggested split into one pull request per approver group, bottom of the stack first, when there is one; each of its file, note and member lists stops at 50 entries, and moreFiles, moreFreeFiles, moreNotes and moreMembers count the rest. Owners named by email are withheld. Pass expectedHeadSha to be refused if the head has moved. Call it once per pull request in a stack.

owner.description: Origin namespace (owner) slug, taken from list_namespaces or an earlier Origin result. A GitHub owner or org name is not an Origin namespace unless list_namespaces returns it.

name.description: Origin repository name within that namespace

expectedHeadSha.description: Refuse with a conflict unless Origin evaluated this head commit
